story.vex: By the time you read this, we already left something behind. Find it, if you can. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED. The backdoor is welded shut. Astro: "Now we know the shape of an attack: in, hide, take, and a door left open for next time. Recognize the shape, and you catch it faster next time."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Volt found something odd overnight. Read logs\breach.log and trace it: how did they get in, where did they hide, and what did they take? Then close the door they left open.
files.C:\\Citadel\\logs\\breach.log:
CITADEL SECURITY LOG · overnight
[03:40] RECON    unknown host scanned the relay port range
[03:47] ENTRY     relay console logged in with a weak, reused password
[03:52] HIDEOUT   a new account 'svc_update' was created, disguised as a system service
[03:58] DATA-GRAB starmap-backup.txt was copied out through port 4477
[04:12] Volt's sensors tripped on the outbound transfer. Connection dropped.

svc_update is not a real Citadel service. Rivet never created it.
The process 'svcupdate.exe' is still listening on port 4477 — that is the door they left open.

steps.title: Trace the break-in
steps.body: Volt: "Every attack has a shape: recon, entry, a hideout, then the grab." Read `logs\breach.log` end to end before touching anything. Notice the planted account and the port it's still listening on.

steps.title: Close the door
steps.body: Rivet: "A hidden account and an open port. Kill both." Disable the planted account with `net user svc_update /active:no`, then stop the process holding the port with `taskkill /im svcupdate.exe /f`. Confirm with `netstat -an` that port 4477 no longer lists.
